why: A period that was never archived must never be purgeable. Without this, an open period -- one still accepting uploads -- could be destroyed.
expectFailing: refuses a period that was never archived

why: Documents inside the retention window must survive, and an instance with no window configured must refuse everything rather than treating 'unset' as 'keep nothing'.
expectFailing: refuses a period inside the retention window

why: A single file under legal hold blocks its whole period. This is the guard with legal consequences if it silently stops working.
expectFailing: refuses when a file in the period is under legal hold

why: Placing or lifting a legal hold must require the periods.manage permission, not merely reach into the file's directory. Without this, anyone who can view a directory could freeze or unfreeze its files' purge eligibility.
expectFailing: refuses a caller with directory access but no periods.manage

why: A legal hold must stop deletion outright. Without this, a file under hold could be trashed like any other, which makes the hold decoration rather than protection.
expectFailing: refuses to trash a file under legal hold

why: An archived period is read-only. Without this, a file created inside an archived period could still be trashed even though it can no longer be replaced or restored.
expectFailing: refuses to trash a file in an archived period

why: Renaming writes back into a file's fixed period exactly as a new version would. Without this, an archived period's files could still be renamed even though new versions and restores are refused.
expectFailing: refuses to rename a file in an archived period

why: Moving writes back into a file's fixed period exactly as a new version would. Without this, an archived period's files could still be moved to another directory even though new versions and restores are refused.
expectFailing: refuses to move a file out of an archived period
